name: Six Seven
description: For positive integers $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$, define $$$f_i(j)$$$ as the maximum integer $$$k$$$ such that $$$i^k$$$ divides $$$j$$$. A number $$$j$$$ is considered special if $$$f_6(j) \gt f_7(j)$$$. For example, $$$6$$$ is special , but $$$67$$$ and $$$7$$$ are not. You are given an array $$$a$$$ of $$$n$$$ positive integers. In one operation, you must increase every element in the array by $$$1$$$. Your task is to find the minimum number of operations needed to make all elements in $$$a$$$ special at the same time, or determine that it is impossible.
input_specification: The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$), the number of test cases. For each test case, the first line contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$). The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$). The sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output a single integer: the minimum number of operations to make all elements special at the same time, or $$$-1$$$ if it is impossible.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2200H — Six Seven [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
